name: Evidence base

subjectOf.text: Increasing the quantity of data does not dissolve the foundational methodological problems of data: construct validity, measurement, reliability, and data dependencies remain the same regardless of how much data is collected.
subjectOf.abstract: Foundational data issues of construct validity, measurement, reliability, and data dependencies are the same regardless of data quantities.
subjectOf.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P. M. Vermeulen, Regulation Tomorrow What Happens When Technology Is Faster Than the Law (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2834531
scope_conditions: where big data is used as a basis for analysis or inference

subjectOf.text: Establishing the facts about a new technology is often impossible in practice because there is no adequate sample or other reliable data on the effects of that technology yet.
subjectOf.abstract: The task of establishing facts about new technology may be made difficult by the lack of an adequate sample or other reliable data on the effects of new technology.
subjectOf.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P. M. Vermeulen, Regulation Tomorrow What Happens When Technology Is Faster Than the Law (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2834531

subjectOf.text: Time pressure produces two distinct fact failures: the facts about a new technology may simply not exist yet, or regulators may select the wrong, contested, or irrelevant facts as the basis of regulation.
subjectOf.abstract: The pressure of time means that the facts surrounding a piece of new technology or other innovation may not be there, or the regulators may simply select the "wrong" — or at least contested or otherwise irrelevant — facts as the basis of regulation.
subjectOf.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P. M. Vermeulen, Regulation Tomorrow What Happens When Technology Is Faster Than the Law (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2834531
scope_conditions: conditions of incessant and accelerating technological change

subjectOf.text: Regulatory experimentation matters within a single jurisdiction and not only across jurisdictions, because it gives regulators data on the real world effects of a particular regulatory scheme in a comparable setting.
subjectOf.abstract: But such experimentation is also important within a particular jurisdiction as it provides regulators with data on the real–world effects of a particular regulatory scheme in a comparable setting.
subjectOf.citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P. M. Vermeulen, Regulation Tomorrow What Happens When Technology Is Faster Than the Law (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2834531
